text: TimeNet Hackathon TimeNet Online Hackathon is live. Pick a time-series problem, onboard a dataset in TimeNet format, then train or fine-tune a Temporal AI Model (e.g. OpenTSLM ) to explore what it can do. Choose any use case, from forecasting and classification to explanation, reasoning and beyond. Register here: challenge.timenet.ai Find, build, and load time-series datasets through one shared format. Note TimeNet is a pre-release project. Its public API and the TimeF format can change before 1.0. Time-series datasets use many incompatible layouts. TimeF gives them one storage format. TimeNet provides one API to find, build, download, and load them. TimeNet handles the data layer. Model training, inference, and evaluation stay in your chosen framework. Register here: challenge.timenet.ai TimeNet needs Python 3.11 or newer. uv add ' timenet[cli] ' uv tool install timenet-connectors timenet-build build timenet/hello-world The build lands in the local registry at ~/.timenet/registry/timenet/hello-world/1.0.0/ . Load it with Python: from timenet import TimeNet dataset = TimeNet (). load ( "timenet/hello-world@1.0.0" ) dataset . describe () signal = dataset . records [ 0 ]. signals [ 0 ] values = signal . to_numpy () TimeNet() reads the local registry first, and the local registry holds this exact version. So the example works without registry credentials or network access. See the Get started guide for installation options and a longer example. A connector converts a raw source into a TimeF version. The version contains: A registry stores immutable TimeF versions. The client reads a version without importing its connector.
